 Judgment

This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act (in short "FSSA") has been filed against the order dated 29/11/2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge, District Morena in M.C.A. No. 32/2024 and order dated 11/03/2024 passed by Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, Morena in Case No. 5/2022/Food Safety.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 07/07/2021 at about 3:30 p.m., the Food Safety Officer collected the samples of Namkeen which were being sold from firm Rathor Namkeen.
It was found that on the back side of the house, the Namkeen is manufactured and is packed.
Appellant, who was present at the time of sampling, disclosed his name as Laxmi Rathor.
He also informed that the Namkeen is being manufactured for sale, and every day, 30 to 35 kg of Namkeen is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31754 2 MSA-8-2025 manufactured by him.
However, no document was produced.

At the time of inspection,
manufacturing of Namkeen and packing were not taking place.
However, 25 packets of Ashok Namkeen Indore were found.
20 kg of besan was also found.
Since the FSO had a suspicion that packing material as well as besan are of a substandard quality, therefore, sample of besan as well as packets over which Ashok Namkeen were printed were collected.

In the report of Food Analyst,
packets containing the print of "AIN Namkeen Ashok Indore" were found misbranded, whereas besan was found within norms.
An information was given along with the report of Food Analyst to appellant, and he was also informed that he can prefer an appeal.

However, no appeal was preferred,

sentences.text: The Adjudicating Officer, after conducting an inquiry, held that appellant is guilty of misbranding the packing material, and accordingly, he was held guilty of committing offense under Section 26(2)(ii) and Section 31(2) read with Sections 52 and 58 of FSSA.

Accordingly, for offense under Section 52 of FSSA, a penalty of 2,00,000/-, and for offense under Section 58 of FSSA, a penalty of 1,00,000/- was imposed.
4. Being aggrieved by the said order, appellant preferred an appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge, District Morena, who by order dated 29/11/2024 dismissed the appeal but interfered with the amount of penalty and a penalty of 2,00,000/- for offense under Section 52 of FSSA was reduced to 1,00,000/- and penalty of 1,00,000/- imposed under Section 58 of FSSA was reduced to 50,000/-, and in all, a total penalty of 1,50,000/- was imposed.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31754 3 MSA-8-2025 5.

Challenging the orders passed by the Food Safety Appellate Authority as well as the Adjudicating Officer, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that since name of his brother is also same,
therefore, it appeared to the FSO that there is a misbranding, but in fact, appellant was selling Namkeen in the name of his brother.

6. Considered the submissions made by counsel for appellant.
7.
Undisputedly, appellant was manufacturing Namkeen in Porsa, District Morena, whereas in the empty packets, in which Namkeen was being packed, it was mentioned as Ashok Indore Namkeen.
Admittedly, neither the appellant nor his brother are based in Indore.
Even if the name of brother of the appellant is Ashok, still they could not have used the word "Indore".
They should have mentioned "Porsa" in place of Indore.

Thus, by misbranding the packet as Ashok Indore Namkeen,
appellant had clearly given a false impression in the mind of the customer that the Namkeen has been produced by the Ashok brand based in Indore.
Thus, defense taken by appellant that there was no misbranding on the part of appellant is misconceived.
8. So far as the quantum of penalty is concerned, First Appellate Court has already shown a sympathetic view which does not require any further interference.

9. Accordingly, order dated 29/11/2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/First District Judge, District Morena in M.C.A. No. 32/2024 and order dated 11/03/2024 passed by Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, Morena in Case No. 5/2022/Food Safety NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31754 4 MSA-8-2025 are hereby affirmed.

sentences.text: 10. At this stage, it is submitted by Shri Prateek Kulshrestha that he may be granted liberty to compound the offense under Section 69 of FSSA.
However, he further submitted that liberty may be granted to the FSO to take a sympathetic view by reducing the quantum of penalty.

sentences.text: Once this Court has already upheld the quantum of penalty as appropriate, then even the FSO will not have any jurisdiction to reduce the amount of penalty in the name of compounding.

Therefore, liberty sought by Shri Prateek Kulshrestha to avail the remedy under Section 69 of FSSA is refused being futile under the facts and circumstances.
12. Appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
